proposed_statement_changes.proposed: There exist constants \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\pi>0\) and a nonempty compact interval \(H_0\subseteq[0,\bar H]\) such that, uniformly for \(h\in H_0\), with probability at least \(\pi+o(1)\) the bounded-Lipschitz distance between the conditional ordinary Efron-bootstrap law of the centered, \(n^{1/4}\)-scaled endpoint pair and its sampling law exceeds \(\varepsilon\). For the exact \(B_n\)-candidate retained algorithm in the retained-bootstrap definition, the same conclusion holds for \(\widehat{\mathbb L}_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\) because its scaled coordinate marginals converge to the random kernel \(\mathcal K_h(Z)\) and its reflection, while \(\sup_{h\in H_0}P_{n,h}(M_n=0)\to0\). Consequently, neither the ordinary conditional endpoint-pair law nor the feasibility-retained conditional endpoint-pair law consistently estimates its sampling law uniformly over the contact-local sequences in \(H_0\). Thus the finite-\(B_n\) feasibility-retained workflow associated with Watson et al.'s Theorem 4 is not contact-uniform as a conditional distributional approximation.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Bounded-Lipschitz separation proves failure of uniform conditional weak consistency, but it does not locate the discrepancy at a preassigned percentile level and therefore does not by itself prove fixed-level percentile coverage failure.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim no longer invokes the retained quantile symbol, and its consumer must state the conditional-distribution conclusion without a fixed-percentile coverage claim.

proposed.justification: A random limiting kernel turns a qualitative boundary warning into a falsifiable nonuniformity theorem for a named implementation.
proposed.gap: Andrews treats a projected boundary estimator and Fang--Santos treat directionally differentiable maps; neither covers the half-Hölder map \(x\mapsto\sqrt{x_+}\) or endogenous retention in leaky-IV bounds.
proposed.consumer: The result shows that ordinary and feasibility-retained resampling are not contact-uniform conditional distributional approximations; coverage of any specified percentile construction requires a separate calibration argument.

prose_updates.related_work: Watson et al. (2024, Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7) supply the unrestricted raw \(p=2\) sharp interval; intersection with \(K\) is imposed by this note. Their Theorem 4 supplies the feasibility-retained endpoint-bootstrap workflow. The exact finite-\(B_n\) Efron algorithm, its negligible zero-retention fallback, the contact endpoint law, retained random kernel, nonuniformity result, score hull, continuous loss elbow, and matched frontiers are not attributed to that paper. Andrews (2000) supplies local boundary-sequence logic, and Fang and Santos (2019) distinguish a regular Gaussian primitive from a nonsmooth transform. Romano and Shaikh (2010) inform the whole-identified-set coverage criterion; Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos (2023) inform constrained-score inversion; and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013) inform multiplier and anti-concentration arguments. The finite-dimensional quadratic-score proof adapted here fully discharged the paper's multiplier question, but only on the strict uniformly regular subclass \(\mathcal P_W\). Hirano and Porter (2012) rule out regular estimation of nondifferentiable functionals; the present Gaussian LAN calculations sharpen that diagnosis to matched fourth-root and root-\(n\) directed-Hausdorff frontiers. Hong and Li's numerical bootstrap regularizes inference for nondifferentiable maps through a tuning/perturbation scheme; it does not deliver the present tuning-free inversion of the regular quadratic score, whole-identified-set coverage, or its explicit contact-to-interior loss elbow. Takatsu and Kuchibhotla provide general local-minimax lower-bound tools for nonsmooth and irregular functionals; the Gaussian LAN converses here are problem-specific two-law-testing counterparts matched to the constructive score-hull upper rates. Staiger and Stock study weak-instrument sequences in which first-stage relevance can vanish, whereas the upper score-hull theorem here assumes relevance uniformly bounded away from zero; no weak-IV robustness is claimed. The bootstrap counterexample and converse witnesses belong to Watson et al.'s broader published \(p=2\) model, whereas the upper hull guarantee does not extend beyond \(\mathcal P_W\).

statement_notes.gap: Numerical-bootstrap regularization, general nonsmooth local-minimax bounds, weak-IV asymptotics, and existing uniform set-coverage or constrained-bootstrap results do not provide this fixed-relevance quadratic-contact whole-set hull and its continuous loss elbow under one score-inversion rule.
